what_this_is: The measured, physical facts MurmurFlow's voice code holds, written down so another voice tool that reuses the same whisper-server setup or vendors murmurflow/speech.py can check itself against them. tests/test_voice_contract.py asserts MurmurFlow's own code still matches this file, so a change that silently diverges from a measurement fails on the day it is made.
why_it_exists: One bug - start_server spawning whisper-server with no cwd, so --convert could not write and the server 500'd on every request - sat in two hand-kept copies of this code and had to be found once and fixed twice. A second (whisper's per-segment newlines reaching the paste) lived in one copy for weeks because nothing compared them. So the MEASUREMENTS are written down, whoever carries the code.
its_honest_limit: This detects a CODE change that diverges from the contract. It does not detect somebody editing this file and the code together, and it cannot see a consumer's copy. Bump `version` when a measurement changes, so a consumer comparing against it sees that it moved.

MIN_CLIP_SECONDS.why: shorter than any word: a brushed key or an aborted chord, never a sentence

SILENT_DBFS.why: a DENIED microphone, not a quiet room. macOS does not fail a denied mic - CoreAudio hands back digital silence - so this separates 'no grant' from 'nobody spoke'. Room tone from a real mic sits near -46 dBFS; true silence is -90 or below.

SPEECH_CONFIDENCE.why: whisper's own detected_language_probability. Measured on large-v3-turbo: every real utterance scored >= 0.969, every silent or noisy clip <= 0.453. 0.75 sits in the empty middle with ~0.22 of margin either side. It is the only gate that catches a fluent invented sentence in an invented language, which no word-list can grow fast enough for.

transcript_seams.rule: A `\n` in a transcript is a whisper SEGMENT boundary, never a line the speaker spoke, and it must be flattened. Flatten it to a SPACE only when there is whitespace on one side of the seam already; when there is none on either side, close it with NOTHING.

transcript_seams.why: whisper segments on the DECODER's budget, which is a token boundary and not a word one, so a seam lands inside a word perhaps once every few sentences. Whisper carries a word's leading space inside its first token, so a segment that begins with no space is the SECOND HALF OF A WORD. Joining every seam with a space typed a domain as `gith ub.io`, and another with its first letter split off, into a real dictation on 2026-08-20. The spacing whisper already emits is the whole signal - there is nothing to measure and nothing to guess.

trailing_hallucination.rule: The boilerplate whisper invents for silence must also be trapped when it is APPENDED to a real sentence, not only when it is the whole transcript. Remove whole trailing sentences that the whole-line trap already recognises; never remove the last sentence standing.
must_hold: Make it public. Thanks for watching!
trailing_hallucination.why: Reported 2026-08-20: `it adds a thank you in the end`. A clip of real speech followed by trailing silence comes back as the sentence PLUS the credit line. Every gate before this one reads the transcript as a whole - the confidence score, the language score and the blocklist all see a confident, real, in-language sentence - so the invented tail passes all three and gets typed.

whisper_warm_request.why: verbose_json is asked for ONLY to get the language score back - the transcript is identical either way. temperature 0 because a dictation is a transcription, not a sample. `prompt` is the proper-noun glossary; dropping it is the difference between 'MurmurFlow' and 'Murmur Flow'.

whisper_server_flags.why: --convert makes whisper-server shell out to ffmpeg, and ffmpeg writes its temp file into the process CWD. Started with no cwd (which is what launchd does - it runs agents at /), the server answers every request with a 500. THIS IS THE BUG THAT SHIPPED IN BOTH COPIES.

ffmpeg_capture.why: aresample=async=1 FILLS dropped avfoundation buffers instead of splicing them out - without it speech plays ~11% fast and whisper transcribes the wrong words. 16k mono is what whisper consumes natively. -flush_packets stops ffmpeg holding ~2s of audio in its buffer.

deliberately_divergent.tidy: MurmurFlow made filler stripping `stripFillers`, default OFF, after it deleted a leading 'hey' from a real sentence, and has since cut every lexical entry from the list - it strips the sounds um/uh/erm/hmm and nothing that is also a word. A consumer whose reader is a language model may strip unconditionally: that reader wants the signal, MurmurFlow's is a human who said those words. Whitespace collapse is NOT in this category - both must flatten whisper's per-segment newlines, because nobody can speak a newline.
deliberately_divergent.hallucination_list: MurmurFlow deliberately narrowed the blocklist; a consumer whose reader can decline to answer may carry a wider one. A false positive deletes a sentence somebody did say, which reads as broken hardware; the confidence gate above subsumes most of it.
deliberately_divergent.quiet_floor: BOTH have QUIET_DBFS (-30.0) now, and they answer DIFFERENT questions with it. MurmurFlow also DROPS a clip whose peak is under the floor, because it types into a document where transcribing a room is worse than losing a sentence; a consumer that hands text to a model that can simply decline to answer may drop nothing, and that half is its own choice. What the shared engine uses the number for is WHERE THE SILENCE IS: has the speaker stopped (the microphone closes itself after SILENCE_STOP_SECONDS) and is this tail worth transcribing (the trailing-quiet trim, without which every self-closed clip ends in silence and comes back with an invented sentence on it). Measured -38 dBFS for a loud silent room and -15 dBFS for the quietest real speech, so -30 sits between them. Do NOT lower it to -40.
